Keep the volume low, at or below the level of your tinnitus and never louder than normal conversation. Loud sound can make tinnitus worse. Stop if you feel discomfort, pressure or pain. The app limits digital peaks, but it cannot know how loud your headphones are, so the safe level is the one that feels comfortable to you.

Tinnitus Relief plays calming sound to make tinnitus less noticeable. It does not diagnose, treat or cure tinnitus. If your tinnitus is new, one-sided, pulsing, or comes with hearing loss or dizziness, see a doctor. No accounts, no ads, no data leaves your phone.
A separate space for exploring personalised sound and recording how your tinnitus responds. It never changes the Relief player.
Lab features are experimental. They are not a clinical measurement or treatment.
Up to three sounds can play together. Remove one first.
Sound could not start. Open the app, check that no call is active and try again.
Combine up to %1$d sounds. Each has its own volume; the main slider sets the overall level.

The Lab plays experimental sounds based on published research. None of them is a proven treatment, and the app does not reproduce any clinical protocol exactly. Every session is time-limited, starts quietly and fades out. Keep the volume low and stop if anything feels uncomfortable.
I understand these sounds are experimental
A subjective estimate made with your own headphones. It is not a clinical measurement.
Use headphones in a quiet room. Set this tone so it is clearly but comfortably audible. You can change it at any time.
Tap A, B or C to listen. Each tone plays for up to 5 seconds, as often as you like. Then select the one closest in pitch to your tinnitus.
Tap Listen and move the slider until the tone matches your tinnitus. Use ½× and 2× to check the octave.
Lower this tone until you can only just hear it. This is your personal reference level.
I can only just hear it
Tap A, B or C to hear three tones at your pitch with different loudness. Then select the one closest in loudness to your tinnitus.
Loudness match: about %1$.0f dB above your own threshold (uncalibrated).
The tone plays continuously. Move the slider until it sounds like your tinnitus, then fine-tune.
Band and gain from published research · filter shape is an engineering choice
Signal generator · no published therapeutic parameters
The studies used calm music. Import your own music in Relief → Sounds to use it here.

Raises two 1/3-octave bands, half an octave below and above your pitch, by 10 dB (Fudan University DFCRS papers, 2025). The exact filters and the \"dynamic\" behaviour are not published, so this is an approximation, not the clinical method.
Removes one octave around your pitch from the sound (Okamoto et al., 2010). Notch depth and edges are engineering choices.
Raises 6–9 kHz by 10 dB regardless of pitch. This was a comparison arm in the MOST trial and did slightly worse than unmodified music. Included for comparison only.
Boost or cut a band of your choice around your pitch. For exploration only.
1/3-octave noise centred on your pitch, as in the MOST trial comparison arm. The level used in the trial was not published.
A steady sine tone at your pitch. A signal generator for exploration, not a treatment.
A tone at your pitch whose loudness pulses. Rate and depth are free settings, not therapeutic values.
A tone at your pitch whose frequency wobbles. Rate and depth are free settings, not therapeutic values.
Sessions always end by themselves, fade in and out, and never resume after an interruption. Lab sound is limited to −6 dB.
Checks whether your tinnitus is quieter for a while after one minute of noise at your pitch.

You will set a narrow-band noise at your pitch so it just covers your tinnitus, rate your tinnitus, listen for 60 seconds, then report what you hear when the noise stops. Classic tests play the noise about 10 dB above the level that just covers the tinnitus.
+10 dB is the value used in the literature. Choose less if it feels too loud. Your phone is not calibrated.
Slowly raise the volume until the noise just covers your tinnitus, and no more.
Listen. Stop at once if it is uncomfortable.
The requested level was above the Lab limit, so it is played at the limit.
Tap when your tinnitus is back to its usual level.
Your tinnitus had not returned after 10 minutes.
A subjective test on uncalibrated headphones. Results vary from day to day.
Rate your tinnitus before a session, right after it and again five minutes later.
Comparing the three ratings shows whether a sound only covers your tinnitus while it plays, or whether some relief lasts afterwards.
Listen as usual. You can lock the phone.
One more rating in five minutes. No notification will be sent.
How noticeable is your tinnitus right now? (0 = not at all, 10 = extremely)
With no sound playing, how noticeable is your tinnitus right now?
One optional rating per day is enough. Long-term trends matter more than single days.

Sound keeps playing with the screen locked. The app uses no network and sleeps completely when paused. On Samsung phones, if playback stops after a long time, set Settings → Apps → Tinnitus Relief → Battery → Unrestricted.

Relief sounds mask tinnitus while they play. The Acoustic Lab adds experimental methods from published studies: DFCRS-inspired band enhancement (Fudan University, 2025), notched sound (Okamoto et al., 2010) and narrow-band noise. In the largest trial (MOST, 2025) the DFCRS group improved by about 4 points more than plain music on a 100-point scale, which is less than the 7 points usually considered clinically meaningful. Complete disappearance of tinnitus was rare. The app does not claim to cure tinnitus.
60 seconds of noise at your pitch
Daily rating, chart and all entries
Let\'s find the version that makes your tinnitus less noticeable.
Both versions play at the same loudness. Keep the volume comfortable and stop if anything feels unpleasant.
No clear preference this time. That is a good answer: the original already suits you.
Both play at the same loudness.
To see which version helps more over several days, use Acoustic Lab → Tests → Original vs personalized.
Which version helps more, over several sessions
Each session plays either the original or your personalized version. The app picks which, in a balanced random order, and tells you only at the end. After several sessions you can compare both.
Listen as usual. Which version is playing stays hidden until the end.
While it plays, how noticeable is your tinnitus?
Now that it has stopped, how noticeable is your tinnitus?
How comfortable was the sound? (0 = unpleasant, 10 = very comfortable)
Changes are average differences from the rating before. Lower while playing means masking, which stops when the sound stops; it is not a lasting improvement.
A sound is playing. Ratings taken while a sound plays measure masking, not your tinnitus itself. Pause first for an accurate daily rating.
Saved as a rating taken while sound was playing. It is not used for the long-term trend.
How much does it bother you today? (optional)
Based on daily ratings with no sound playing. Masking and residual inhibition are shown separately because they are temporary.
A trend needs at least 4 weeks with 3 or more ratings each. So far: %1$d.
About the same as at the start: %1$.1f → %2$.1f
Compares the first two and the last two qualifying weeks. A change of less than 1 point is treated as no change. This does not show what caused a change.
Self-reported tinnitus-free weeks in a row: %1$d
How sure are you about this match?
Repeating the match on different days makes the estimate more reliable.
Experimental. Sound is disabled in this version until the acoustic calibration and safety review are complete. You can prepare everything and rehearse sessions silently.

A research sound from a published trial (Yukhnovich et al., 2025): a soft buzzing tone with a slow ripple in the frequency band chosen from your tinnitus pitch. In that trial, tinnitus became slightly quieter on average. It is not a proven treatment and no cure.

Runs the full session without any sound

These questions come from the trial\'s exclusion rules and common medical warning signs. Any \"yes\" means this sound is not suitable for you without a clinician\'s advice.
Has your tinnitus ever got worse after moderately loud sounds?
Do everyday sounds often feel too loud or painful?
Does your tinnitus beat in time with your pulse?
Have you had sudden hearing loss or a sudden change in hearing in the last 3 months?
Is your tinnitus new and in one ear only?
Do you have ear pain, discharge from the ear, or dizziness?
Not suitable without a clinician\'s advice. Please talk to a doctor or audiologist.
The trial offered four versions with extra high-frequency level (0, 15, 30, 45 dB) for people with high-frequency hearing loss. You would choose the one in which all test tones sound equally loud.
30 and 45 dB are locked until an audiologist has reviewed them.
Listening checks need sound, which is disabled until calibration.
In the trial, an alternative band was used if any tone inside the main band could not be heard. You will hear each tone once and answer heard / not heard.

The plan follows the trial: two 6-week listening periods, each followed by a 3-week break. One period uses the real sound, the other a comparison sound that modulates a band far from your tinnitus. The app chooses the order at random and hides it until the end, so your ratings are not influenced. Rate your tinnitus every day with no sound playing.
The two sounds are similar but not identical: their spectra differ by about 2 dB in different octaves, so you might notice a difference.
Tap again to show the order
Tap again to end the plan
Silent rehearsal: no sound is produced. Rehearsals do not count as listening.
Up to %1$d min. The sound starts silent and fades in; it never gets louder by itself. Any interruption ends the session.
Rate with no sound playing. This is also used for your daily rating.
Use the lowest level at which you can clearly hear the sound. It should never be uncomfortable.
Now, with no sound playing, how noticeable is your tinnitus?
Did you notice any of these?
Any symptom pauses listening until a clinician has checked it.
Listening is paused because symptoms were reported. Please see a doctor or audiologist before continuing.
Listening is paused for at least 24 hours because your tinnitus was 2 or more points louder after the session.
Ratings with no sound playing, averaged over 7 days at the start and end of each listening period and at the end of its break. The sound used in each period is shown only after the plan ends.
A personal result can be due to chance, expectation or natural change. It does not prove that the sound works.

Up to %1$d min per session, at least %2$d min between sessions, at most %3$d min per 24 hours. Every session starts silent and fades in, never gets louder by itself, and stops on any interruption (call, headphones unplugged, other audio, output change).
A clinician has checked my symptoms
